Commentary.Commentary: Right then, the Umpires are out and the Afghanistan Under-19 fielders are seen in a hurdle. The players now take their field positions and the opening pair of Arjun Kumal and Bipin Rawal for Nepal Under-19 walk into the middle. Faridoon Dawoodzai has the new ball in hand is raring to go. Let's play says the Umpire!
... RUN CHASE ...

Afghanistan Under-19's batting struggles persisted in today's match, mirroring their previous performances. Opting to bat after winning the toss, Afghanistan Under-19 faced early setbacks with two wickets falling for a mere 2 runs on the scoreboard. While Hassan Eisakhil provided a stabilizing presence and contributed decently, his efforts were cut short by Aakash Chand. The middle order, however, succumbed to the formidable bowling attack of Nepal Under-19. In the face of this collapse, Allah Mohammad emerged as the linchpin, launching a counter-attack with a quickfire 37 off 21 balls. Post that a crucial determined 9th wicket partnership between skipper Naseer Khan Maroofkhil and Faridoon Dawoodzai adding 55 runs towards the end salvaged Afghanistan Under-19 to a competitive total. Reflecting on their past performance, Afghanistan Under-19 will draw confidence from almost defending 91 runs in their second game against New Zealand. The Afghan bowlers will aim to replicate that stellar performance, posing a potential challenge for Nepal U-19. Will Afghanistan Under-19 make the pursuit difficult for Nepal Under-19, or will it be a straightforward chase for Nepal to advance into the super-sixes round? Let's find out as the chase comes to you in a bit.

It has been a day of Aakash Chand. Having put into the field first, the Nepal Under-19 bowlers executed their game plan impeccably, consistently delivering tight lines and lengths that denied any batting opposition the luxury of settling in. The opening salvo saw Gulshan Jha making an impact in the very first over, dismissing Numan Shah for a golden duck. Aakash Chand, operating from the other end, mirrored the feat by sending Khalid Taniwal back to the pavilion without scoring. Unrelenting in his performance, Aakash Chand continued to apply pressure, orchestrating the dismissal of three more batters with the scoreboard displaying a collective void. His resilient display reached its pinnacle when he claimed the prized wicket of Hassan Eisakhil, securing a well-deserved five-wicket haul. The spin maestro, Tilak Bhandari, intervened to curtail Allah Mohammad's valiant resistance, swinging the momentum back in favour of Nepal Under-19 and firmly placing them in the driver's seat. Although a great resilient innings between the skipper Naseer Khan Maroofkhil and Faridoon Dawoodzai might have rattled things a bit pushing Nepal Under-19 on the backfoot, Dipesh Kandel and Subash Bhandari succeeded in breaking the annoying partnership and finishing things off.

It has been an entertaining first phase of play and Afghanistan Under-19 conclude their innings with 145 runs on the board. Despite a challenging start, they have managed to reach a competitive total they will fancy defending with the kind of bowling attack at their disposal.
